info.title: Luma public API
info.description: Read your workspace’s orders, fulfillment, stock, products, customers, returns, issues, workflows and activity with a personal API app token. Send it as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. A token works in one workspace, with the permissions it was granted that its creator still holds. Requests are limited per token and per workspace: responses report the tighter limit in `RateLimit-Limit`, `RateLimit-Remaining` and `RateLimit-Reset`, and a 429 response says when to retry in `Retry-After`. Reads of operations marked `x-luma-personal-data` by a token that can read customers are counted and recorded in the workspace’s activity.

apiToken.description: A personal API app token, created in workspace settings. It acts for the person who created it, limited to the permissions they chose, in one workspace.

get.description: List issues that need a person, active work or history. `where` takes conditions on the issues catalog fields, such as class, state, owner, source, attention reason, freshness, diagnosis, resolution, record type and dates; `q` searches summaries and records. Results sort by urgency by default: severity, then the oldest attention request or detection, then ID. `group` returns each group’s count and first rows. Freshness is fresh only while the investigation’s evidence is still valid; stale and unknown evidence are never reported as fresh. Use the returned cursor with the same query. Refresh from the first page as cases change.

schema.description: Issues of one owner, or `unassigned`. Kept for older links; prefer an `owner` condition.
Matches the summary, the record ID or its type, ignoring case. Never stored in saved views.
JSON-encoded conditions: `{"match":"all"|"any","conditions":[{"field","op","value","source"}]}`. Fields and operators follow the list catalog; unsupported combinations return 400.
Group rows by a field, such as `status` or `placed:week`. Each group returns its count and its first rows.
JSON-encoded group key from `groups[].key`, such as `"open"`, `true` or `null`, to read more rows of one group. Requires `group`.
Rows returned per group, from 1 to 50.
Days, weeks and months in conditions such as `today` or `within_last`, and date groups, follow this time zone.

`urgency` puts high severity first, then the oldest attention request, or the oldest detection for issues that need nobody. `waitingSince` is when the issue started waiting on a person; issues that wait on nobody come last in both directions.
Defaults to ascending for `urgency` and `waitingSince`, descending for `detected` and `lastActivity`.

groups.description: With `group`: each group in display order with its exact count and first rows, whose issues are in `items`. With `groupKey`: the one group, with this page of its rows. An issue with several sources counts in each source’s group.

groupsTruncated.description: More than 50 groups match; narrow the conditions to see the rest.

get.description: Returns persisted observation and verification references ordered by immutable ID, including evidence outside the current diagnosis. Pages default to 25 references and allow at most 100. Reuse cursors only for the same organization, case and page size. As evidence arrives, refresh from the first page and deduplicate by ID. Completeness is unknown unless explicitly recorded for the observation. A null source update time means unknown, regardless of observation freshness.

Returns the current persisted investigation and up to 100 evidence references. Use the evidence endpoint to read further historical references. Recommendations require review; they do not authorize execution. Unavailable cases return not found.
Returns your membership, role and effective permissions. Changes to your role apply on the next request.

Searches persisted return cases by case, order, source identity or item. Customer filtering also requires customers.read and follows source order mappings. No provider is called. The cursor is bound to the tenant and filters.

Requires `returns.read`. Reads a return case with its lines, the receipt, inspection and proposed resolution with who decided them and on which evidence, the case history, and the latest request to create the return in the order’s system.

List customer profiles imported from connected stores. Each profile belongs to one connection and source customer; profiles are never merged across stores, and names or email addresses do not establish identity. Name, email and phone are null unless the source shares contact details (`shared.contact`). `orderCount` and `amountSpent` are what the source reports. Search matches the name, email address, phone number and source customer ID. `externalId` with `connectionId` finds one source customer. Conditions (`where`) and grouping (`group`) use the Customers catalog fields, and conditions and sorting also accept readable custom customer fields as `custom:<field ID>`; a country the source does not share is unknown and never matches a country condition, and amounts compare only within one currency. The last order date needs access to orders. `sources` lists each commerce connection and whether it shares customers with Luma. Results contain up to `limit` profiles (at most 50) with `totalCount` matches; nextCursor continues the same filters, conditions, grouping and sorting.

schema.description: JSON-encoded conditions: `{"match":"all"|"any","conditions":[{"field","op","value","source"}]}`. Fields and operators follow the list catalog; unsupported combinations return 400.
Group rows by a field, such as `status` or `placed:week`. Each group returns its count and its first rows.
JSON-encoded group key from `groups[].key`, such as `"open"`, `true` or `null`, to read more rows of one group. Requires `group`.
Rows returned per group, from 1 to 50.
Days, weeks and months in conditions such as `today` or `within_last`, and date groups, follow this time zone.

`amountSpent` orders by currency, then amount, so amounts compare only within one currency. `updated` is the source’s last change. `lastOrder` needs access to orders. `custom:<field ID>` sorts by a readable custom customer field that holds one value. Customers without a value come last in both directions.
Accepted for every list; customer counts are always exact.

missingSince.description: When a complete read of the source first no longer found this customer; null while the source still has them. Luma removes customers that stay missing for 30 days.

country.description: Country of the shared address as the source reports it, upper-cased; null when the source shares no address or reports no country.

lastOrderAt.description: Latest placed date of the imported orders this source attributes to the customer; null when none reports one. Omitted without access to orders.

groups.description: With `group`: each group in display order with its exact count, first rows (whose items are in `items`) and per-currency amounts spent. With `groupKey`: the one group, with this page of its rows. `complete` is false while a source is still importing its customers.

groupsTruncated.description: More than 50 groups match; narrow the conditions to see the rest.

get.description: Read one imported customer profile with its address, when the source shares addresses, and the connection it came from. Order history is read live through the connected app.

missingSince.description: When a complete read of the source first no longer found this customer; null while the source still has them. Luma removes customers that stay missing for 30 days.

country.description: Country of the shared address as the source reports it, upper-cased; null when the source shares no address or reports no country.

lastOrderAt.description: Latest placed date of the imported orders this source attributes to the customer; null when none reports one. Omitted without access to orders.

get.description: Lists fulfillment orders and shipments as each connected source currently reports them. `attention` returns held, delayed and failed fulfillments; `held` returns open work stopped by a source hold; `delayed` returns open work past its fulfill-by date or without progress for `stalledAfterHours`, and shipments with a reported delivery problem or past their estimated delivery; `open` returns work still expected; `in_transit` returns shipped, undelivered shipments. Search matches order numbers, tracking numbers, location names and source order or fulfillment IDs. Mirrored work in different systems stays separate. Conditions (`where`) and grouping (`group`) use the Fulfillment catalog fields and also narrow the per-view counts; holds a source does not report are unknown and match no comparison. Results contain up to `limit` fulfillments (at most 50) with counts per view; `nextCursor` continues the same filters, conditions, grouping, sort and evaluation time.

schema.description: JSON-encoded conditions: `{"match":"all"|"any","conditions":[{"field","op","value","source"}]}`. Fields and operators follow the list catalog; unsupported combinations return 400.
Group rows by a field, such as `status` or `placed:week`. Each group returns its count and its first rows.
JSON-encoded group key from `groups[].key`, such as `"open"`, `true` or `null`, to read more rows of one group. Requires `group`.
Rows returned per group, from 1 to 50.
Days, weeks and months in conditions such as `today` or `within_last`, and date groups, follow this time zone.

`waiting` and `recent` order by last progress. `deadline` orders work with a deadline first, then the rest by last progress. Other sorts use their field; rows without a value come last in both directions.
Defaults to the sort’s natural direction: descending for `recent` and `orderPlaced`, ascending otherwise.
Accepted for every list; fulfillment counts are always exact.

groups.description: With `group`: each group in display order with its exact count and first rows, whose items are in `items`. With `groupKey`: the one group, with this page of its rows. `complete` is false while a source is still importing its fulfillment history.

groupsTruncated.description: More than 50 groups match; narrow the conditions to see the rest.

get.description: Returns one fulfillment with its lines, order, up to 50 of the order’s other fulfillments, up to 50 observed source states (newest first), linked issues, workflow runs and recent Luma activity. A workflow run’s `progressObservedAt` is the first later read showing the order shipped or its work completed; a method correction or an accepted source request alone does not establish progress.

Search SKUs and locations and compare current stock quantities by source. Quantities are never added across sources. Null means unknown. Results contain up to `limit` positions, by SKU and location unless sorted otherwise; nextCursor continues the same filters and sort. Source filters select positions while retaining all sources for comparison.

schema.description: Quantities sort by the lowest value any source reports; sources that report none are ignored. `lastRead` is the most recent read of any source. Positions without a value come last in both directions. Ties continue by SKU, location and position ID.
Request the exact number of matches. Without this option, totalCount is null.

Group rows by a field, such as `status` or `placed:week`. Each group returns its count and its first rows.
JSON-encoded group key from `groups[].key`, such as `"open"`, `true` or `null`, to read more rows of one group. Requires `group`.

get.description: Compare sources for one SKU, location and unit. Includes up to 100 observed snapshots and 50 entries per related record type. Orders and purchase orders relate to the SKU; they do not confirm location allocation or incoming supply. Incoming quantities and distinct provider stock states remain unknown until reported. Location activity, item activation and tracking are separate facts; quantities do not establish sellability.

bundleContext.description: Catalog context of a known bundle parent. Its timestamp is independent of the stock read and does not establish physical component stock.
Catalog context of a known bundle parent. Its timestamp is independent of the stock read and does not establish physical component stock.

get.description: Lists current orders from your connected sources. Search matches order numbers, source order IDs, SKU text on order lines and source SKU IDs. Filter by status, payment, source, customer, placed or updated time, or a saved view, and combine conditions from the Orders field catalog with `where`; an unsupported field, operator or value returns 400 naming the condition. Missing or unknown values never match a comparison such as `lineCount eq 0`, and amounts only match in the currency you name. Relative dates such as `today` or the last 7 days use `timeZone`. Warehouse and stock-blocked conditions need access to fulfillment (stock-blocked also to inventory), and customer conditions access to customers; without it they return 403. Outstanding, overdue and needs-you views count the same orders as the order metrics. Sorting puts orders without a value last in either direction; `total` orders by currency, then amount. Pass `group` to receive each group with its exact count, first rows and per-currency totals, and `groupKey` with that group’s `nextCursor` to read more of one group. Conditions, grouping and the newer sorts return 503 while order data is being rebuilt or your access to sources is restricted. Pass `count=exact` to include the total number of matches; otherwise `totalCount` is null. Results use `nextCursor` for the following page; a cursor is only valid with the filters, grouping and sort that produced it, and any other cursor returns 400 with a message to start from the first page.

schema.description: Request the exact number of matches. Without this option, totalCount is null.
Canonical fulfillment warehouse. Requires fulfillment access.
Open orders with an explicit source inventory-out-of-stock hold observed within five minutes. Missing or stale holds remain unknown. Requires inventory and fulfillment access.
Imported customer ID: only orders the source attributes to this customer. Requires access to customers.
JSON-encoded conditions: `{"match":"all"|"any","conditions":[{"field","op","value","source"}]}`. Fields and operators follow the list catalog; unsupported combinations return 400.
Group rows by a field, such as `status` or `placed:week`. Each group returns its count and its first rows.
JSON-encoded group key from `groups[].key`, such as `"open"`, `true` or `null`, to read more rows of one group. Requires `group`.
Rows returned per group, from 1 to 50.
Days, weeks and months in conditions such as `today` or `within_last`, and date groups, follow this time zone.

Missing values sort last in both directions. `total` orders by currency code, then amount, both in the sort direction; amounts in different currencies are never compared. Status, payment and fulfillment follow their documented option order. `custom:<field ID>` sorts by a readable custom order field that holds one value.

get.description: List SKUs from the connected catalogs and compare each source’s title, status, listing, price and barcode. No source is treated as authoritative. `differs` returns SKUs whose sources disagree; `missing` returns SKUs absent from at least one catalog source; `unlinked` returns SKUs with an unlinked SKU of the same code in another source. Prices are compared only within the same reported currency. Results contain up to `limit` SKUs (at most 50) with counts per view; nextCursor continues the same filters and sort.

schema.description: `rank`: SKUs with a code first, then SKUs with only a title, each alphabetically. `price`: the lowest listed price in the alphabetically first currency any listing reports, so amounts compare only within one currency; prices without a currency are ignored. `updated`: the most recent source update of any listing. `differences` and `listings` count the differing fields and current listings. `custom:<field ID>` sorts by a readable custom product field that holds one value. SKUs without a value come last in both directions.
Accepted for every list; product counts are always exact.
JSON-encoded conditions: `{"match":"all"|"any","conditions":[{"field","op","value","source"}]}`. Fields and operators follow the list catalog; unsupported combinations return 400.
Group rows by a field, such as `status` or `placed:week`. Each group returns its count and its first rows.
JSON-encoded group key from `groups[].key`, such as `"open"`, `true` or `null`, to read more rows of one group. Requires `group`.
Rows returned per group, from 1 to 50.
Days, weeks and months in conditions such as `today` or `within_last`, and date groups, follow this time zone.

counts.description: Matching SKUs per built-in view under the current search, source filters and conditions.

groups.description: With `group`: each group in display order with its exact count and first SKUs, whose items are in `items`. A SKU with several vendors or statuses counts in each of their groups. With `groupKey`: the one group, with this page of its SKUs.

groupsTruncated.description: More than 50 groups match; narrow the conditions to see the rest.

get.description: Compare one SKU across sources and see what depends on it: other variants, up to 50 observed listing snapshots, stock positions, units ordered in the last 30 days per source, orders, purchase orders and issues (up to 50 each). Sales are not added across sources because systems can mirror the same order. Purchase orders are commitments, not confirmed incoming stock.

bundleContext.description: Catalog context of a known bundle parent. Its timestamp is independent of the stock read and does not establish physical component stock.

get.description: List returns imported from connected stores, and refunds that no return settles, with their stage and refund state. `action` returns need a person: a request to review, units to refund, a failed refund payment or a return to close. `waiting` returns wait for items or a processing refund payment; `done` returns are closed, declined, cancelled or refunded. `refund.refunded` sums successful refund payments only; pending and failed payments are reported separately and never count as money returned. `sources` lists each commerce connection and whether it shares returns with Luma. Search matches the return name, order number, return reason and source IDs, and for readers with customer access the name and email address of the order’s customer when the source shares them. Conditions (`where`) and grouping (`group`) use the Returns catalog fields and also narrow the counts; receipt a source does not report is unknown and matches no comparison, and amounts compare only within one currency. Results contain up to `limit` records (at most 50) with counts per view and stage; nextCursor continues the same filters, conditions, grouping and sorting.

schema.description: JSON-encoded conditions: `{"match":"all"|"any","conditions":[{"field","op","value","source"}]}`. Fields and operators follow the list catalog; unsupported combinations return 400.
Group rows by a field, such as `status` or `placed:week`. Each group returns its count and its first rows.
JSON-encoded group key from `groups[].key`, such as `"open"`, `true` or `null`, to read more rows of one group. Requires `group`.
Rows returned per group, from 1 to 50.
Days, weeks and months in conditions such as `today` or `within_last`, and date groups, follow this time zone.

`value` and `pendingRefund` order by currency, then amount, so amounts compare only within one currency. `stage` follows the return lifecycle from requested to closed, then by request time. Returns without a value come last in both directions.
Accepted for every list; return counts are always exact.

groups.description: With `group`: each group in display order with its exact count, first rows (whose items are in `items`) and per-currency value sums. With `groupKey`: the one group, with this page of its rows. `complete` is false while a source is still importing its returns.

groupsTruncated.description: More than 50 groups match; narrow the conditions to see the rest.

get.description: Read one return with its items, reasons, receipt and refund quantities, refunds with every payment attempt, the order it belongs to, other returns of that order and up to 50 observed snapshots. The ID of a refund that settles a return resolves to that return. Store returns are read-only here; work them in a return case, and approve, receive and refund them in the source store.

The `business` view groups events by issue, run or proposal and hides routine checks; `detail=steps` includes up to 100 earlier steps under the same visibility and filters. The default event view retains each immutable record. Returns recorded events newest first by recorded timestamp and immutable ID. Date bounds apply to recorded time, including from and excluding to, for at most 366 days. Search matches issue ID, issue class, persisted target reference, action label, actor ID and workflow run ID (literal, case-insensitive substring), and events of the issue classes named in `searchIssueClasses`. Raw payloads are not searched. `actor` keeps events recorded by any of the named actors and `outcome` keeps events with any of the named outcomes; both only narrow what the caller may already see. Cursors are bound to workspace, restricted-activity access, filters and page size; any other cursor returns 400 with a message to start from the first page. Connection changes and access changes (members, invitations, roles and workspace settings, type `access`) are visible only with the View restricted activity permission; `visibility` is `admin` for those callers. Approval and provider acceptance do not establish verified resolution.

schema.description: Comma-separated issue classes, such as `stuck_fulfillment`, whose names match `q` in the reader’s language. Events of these classes match the search too, so clients can search by translated issue names.

Comma-separated outcomes, matching any, such as `failed,uncertain,escalated`. Outcomes: `approved`, `rejected`, `escalated`, `attempted`, `provider_accepted`, `verified`, `failed`, `uncertain`, `manually_disposed`, `recorded`.

Comma-separated actors, matching any: `me` (the reader), `luma` (Luma and Luma support), `workflow` (events a workflow run recorded) or user IDs. A person also matches workflow runs that act for them.
Returns only the group, or in the event view the event, with this event ID, under the same filters. The group may hold the event as an earlier step. Takes no cursor.

get.description: Requires `workflows.read`. People can inspect published versions and activation status. Viewing a workflow never activates it.
Read published steps, versions, prerequisites and historical grants. Process versions show the exact order of decisions, actions, waits and verification.

Returns the 50 most recent runs with subject, actor, trigger and step evidence, and the names of the people who started them. Process runs show their current state and recorded outputs. Execution and verification results are separate.
